---
title: Edit Resource Properties
description: Read and change typed property values on an existing resource.
---

# Edit Resource Properties

Property values are read through the resource schema and changed through a
resource builder. Editing a schema you fetched from a query does not persist
anything by itself.

For the complete set of access forms, including step parameters, see
[Property and Parameter Access](../reference/property-and-parameter-access.qmd).

## Read values

```python
plate = namespace.query_maker().resources().filter(name="Plate 001").first()

rows = plate.properties.dimensions.rows.value
unit = plate.properties.dimensions.rows.unit
```

The trailing `.value` is required. Without it you get the wrapper object that
holds the value and its unit, which prints like the value but does not compare
equal to it.

Bracket access accepts either the normalized slug or the original attribute
name, and `.get(name)` returns `None` for a missing attribute instead of
raising:

```python
group = plate.properties["dimensions"]

rows = group["rows"].value
rows = group.get("rows").value
```

## Change values on a mutable resource

Assign the raw value inside a builder block. There is no `.value` on the
left-hand side:

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id) as builder:
    builder.resource.properties.dimensions.rows = 16
```

The builder validates values against the template and persists the aggregate on
successful context-manager exit. An exception rolls the change back.

## Change values on an active resource

::: {.callout-important}
## Edits to an active resource go to a copy by default

A resource becomes frozen once it is `ACTIVE`. Saving builder edits to it
creates a new mutable copy that records its origin; the original is
unchanged. Because queries return only active resources, any resource you
located with a query is already frozen.
:::

To change the active resource itself, opt in to editing in place:

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=plate.id, in_place=True) as builder:
    builder.resource.properties.dimensions.rows = 16
```

The resource keeps its ID and status and its revision increments. Process
runs that reference it see the new values.

To keep the original and work on a revision instead, copy it explicitly:

```python
from recap import ResourceCopyOptions

copied = namespace.copy_resource(
    source_resource_id=plate.id,
    options=ResourceCopyOptions(name="Plate 001 Revision"),
)

with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=copied.id) as builder:
    builder.resource.properties.dimensions.rows = 16
    builder.finalize()
```

The copy records its origin, so lineage from the revision back to the original
is preserved. See
[Manage Resource Lifecycle](manage-resource-lifecycle.qmd) for both
procedures.

## Units and metadata

Setting a value preserves the attribute's existing unit. Set the unit
explicitly when an update changes its meaning:

```python
with namespace.build_resource(resource_id=copied.id) as builder:
    builder.resource.properties.dimensions.rows = 16
    builder.resource.properties.dimensions.rows.unit = "count"
```

Template metadata can constrain numeric ranges or enumerate allowed values.
Invalid values fail validation before the mutation is committed.
